# Studienstiftung des deutschen Volkes – Overview
**Studienstiftung des deutschen Volkes** is Germany’s largest and oldest scholarship foundation, offering general scholarships for bachelor’s, master’s, and PhD students at German, EU, or Swiss universities. Founded in 1925, dissolved under National Socialism in 1934, and re-established in 1948, the Studienstiftung selects exceptionally talented and responsible students through nominations by schools, professors, examination boards, competition winners, an assessment test, alumni, and for arts/music candidates through special processes. Eligibility is not restricted by citizenship or age, though recipients must study full-time and at least partially at a German/EU/Swiss institution.

# Scholarship Benefits and Program Details
Studienstiftung scholarships include financial support—an allowance of €300 per month plus need-based supplements up to €855 monthly for undergraduates and graduates, and €1,550 to €1,650 monthly plus research allowance for PhD scholars. Additional funds are available for students with children, and study abroad is supported. Academic support encompasses summer schools, workshops, mentoring, and opportunities for scholars to organize academic events. Internal and open scholarship programs are available, and the Studienstiftung collaborates with other organizations for select opportunities. In 2023, the foundation supported nearly 15,000 scholars (including doctoral students), representing approximately 0.48% of German students, with prominent alumni across sciences, arts, business, politics, and journalism.
